author: n-gao
body:
This PR replaces the symmetric centered-stencil image replication with a pair-anchored window approach, fixing correctness on skewed triclinic cells and reducing over-replication. The benefits of this are purely performance and memory improvements.

## Image replication: anchored windows instead of symmetric stencils

Previously, `candidate_image_counts` computed a symmetric stencil of width `2 * ceil(ratio) + 1` centered at the origin, and `_generate_image_offsets` returned origin-centered coordinates. This over-counted images (e.g., ratio 0.8 produced 3 images/axis = 27 copies instead of the tight 2/axis = 8) and could miss the true closest image on highly skewed cells where round-based minimum-image shifts pick the wrong copy.

The new approach:

- `candidate_image_counts` returns `floor(2 * ratio) + 1` — the exact count of lattice planes a sphere of radius `cutoff` can reach along each axis.
- `_generate_image_offsets` now emits 0-based window coordinates (no origin centering), with the window center emitted first as a stable tie-break.
- `_get_candidate_images` anchors each candidate's window at `ceil(separation - ratio)`, which provably brackets every in-range periodic image of that pair. The `queries` table is now a required argument to compute per-pair separations.
- The `has_been_replicated` flag is removed. Instead, `_minimum_image_mask` uses a segment argmin over real distances to identify the closest copy per original candidate — correct even on acute/skewed cells where rounding fails.
- `replicate_for_images` no longer blends MIC shifts with image shifts; it passes the anchored offsets directly and delegates minimum-image detection entirely to `_minimum_image_mask`.

## Single-cell fast path in `_cell_list_subselect`

When `max_num_cells.size == 1`, every particle maps to the same cell and the stencil expansion is unnecessary. A new `single_cell` branch skips the vmap stencil tiling and the `jnp.unique` deduplication step, and passes `is_sorted=False` to `subselect` since the hashes are no longer pre-sorted by `unique`.

## Tests

- Updated `TestCandidateImageCounts`, `TestReplicateForImages`, `TestGetCandidateImagesIsFinite`, and `TestGenerateImageOffsets` to reflect the new window widths and 0-based coordinates.
- Added `test_single_cell_path_matches_multi_cell_path` verifying the single-cell fast path emits the same candidate set as the general path.
- Added `test_triclinic_images.py` with brute-force completeness and minimum-image flag tests across orthogonal, monoclinic, acute (35°), and anisotropic short-axis cells, exercising the full pipeline via `DenseNearestNeighborList` and `replicate_for_images` directly.

Protects the `source_type` invariant that makes set removal safe. Runs against a real on-disk SQLite file under `tmp_path` with foreign keys enforced (exactly as `db.get_connection` does in production).

## The crown-jewel test
**Removal invariant** — seed two owned sets with generated `full_set` entries, a `manual` single, and an `override` entry *deliberately tagged* `source_set_code='neo'`. Then `remove_owned_set('neo')`:
- deletes **only** NEO's two `full_set` rows (returns `2`) and the NEO `owned_sets` row;
- the manual single, the override (despite its `neo` tag), and MOM's generated entry all **survive**.

That proves removal is guarded by `source_type`, not `source_set_code` — the override surviving is the whole point.

author: vyseclown
body:
## Summary

Closes a concurrency window in the lock primitive. Locks took ownership with a `mkdir` gate **then** a separate `printf $$ >pid` write; between those steps a concurrent claimant could see a pid-less lock dir, judge it stale (`lock_is_stale` treats a missing pid as stale), reclaim it, and become a **second owner** — corrupting `run.lock` state or handing two parallel runs the same simulator.

- New **`atomic_lock_acquire`**: the ownership token is the pid file, created with **O_EXCL** via `set -C` (noclobber). A lock is never observable without its owner pid; the dir is just a metadata container. Dead-pid locks are still reclaimed, and the reclaim re-create is also O_EXCL so only one racing reclaimer wins.
- Applied at **all three** lock sites: `acquire_lock` (run.lock), `device_try_claim`, and the clone-create `.creating` marker.

This is the "design concurrency in, not on" follow-through from the engine review.

## Test Plan
- [x] New `fixture_atomic_lock`: fresh-win, live-contention rejection, dead-pid reclaim, and the formerly-racy **pid-less dir** case (dir alone never confers ownership).
- [x] Existing `fixture_run_lock` + all device-registry fixtures still green (behavior preserved).

author: n-gao
body:
Stacks leaf arrays using `jnp.stack` via a JIT-compiled helper (`_stack_leaves`) instead of individually converting each leaf with `np.stack`/`np.asarray` per step. This batches the stacking work on the accelerator before a single `np.asarray` transfer to the host, reducing overhead when flushing buffered states to HDF5.

Furthermore we default to zstd instead of gzip for higher throughput at lower file sizes.

The default chunk/batch size target is also increased from 1 MiB to 4 MiB to better amortize I/O and JIT dispatch costs.

It now splits the content into graphemes, matching `Str.comb` with no args and Rakudo. The `None`-for-no-arg semantics are shared with the generic caller, so the fix is kept local to the IO::Path comb helper.

With this slice the whole **IO::Path FS method family (stat / content-read / fs-mutate / open / two-path / comb) is VM-native** — §D ③'s IO native work is complete.

author: hackerwins
body:
## Summary

Fixes three issues on slide 10 of an imported Google-Slides deck, plus a build-time table that generalizes the text-rect fix to all preset shapes.

1. **Cloud shape** — `buildCloud` was a 6-lobe heuristic that read differently from PowerPoint. Replaced it with a verbatim port of the OOXML `cloud` preset (11 elliptical-arc bumps from `presetShapeDefinitions.xml`), mapped to the frame with a per-axis scale. Also fixed the jsdom test-canvas shim to sample partial elliptical arcs (it modelled every `ellipse()` as a full disc), with snapshot churn confined to the 6 partial-arc shapes.

2. **Timeline arrows pointed the wrong way** — the two short arrows are `straightConnector1`s with `flipH=1` + `rot=180°` (which cancel on a horizontal line, so PowerPoint points them right). Connectors render from stored world-coordinate endpoints with no frame transform, but the PPTX importer's `resolveEndpoint` baked in the flip and **dropped the rotation**, landing the arrowhead on the wrong endpoint. It now composes flip-then-rotate about the frame centre (reduces exactly to the old corner-swap when rotation is 0).

3. **Inline text was left-shifted in the cloud** — the paragraph is genuinely `algn="l"`; it reads centred in PowerPoint only because PowerPoint lays text inside the preset's inset `<rect>` (cloud: ~13.8% left / 20.9% right). wafflebase used one uniform padding for every shape. Added a per-`ShapeKind` text rectangle composed with the default padding, routed through both the renderer and the editor's edit-frame so paint and caret stay aligned.

4. **Generalized to all presets (build-time table)** — rather than hand-maintain ~137 inset rects, `scripts/gen-shape-text-rects.mjs` resolves every preset's `<rect>` from the canonical `presetShapeDefinitions.xml` via a small DrawingML guide-formula evaluator and emits `shape-text-rects.generated.ts` (119 kinds). Full-frame, degenerate (`pie`), and the canonical file's typo'd `leftArrow` source are omitted; `upDownArrow` (defined twice) is de-duped; `homePlate`→`pentagonArrow`. `pnpm slides gen:textrects` regenerates; a unit test pins known fractions and runs the generator in `--check` mode to fail on drift.

> **Note:** the cloud silhouette and text centering are render-time (apply on reload). The arrow direction was resolved at import time and is baked into existing stored docs — the live deck needs a **re-import** to pick that up.

## Test plan

- `pnpm verify:fast` green (2282 slides tests).
- New tests: connector flipH+rot=180° import; cloud preset text-rect inset; generated-table values + `--check` drift guard.
- Real-browser render check (Canvas2D): cloud silhouette matches PowerPoint; all 4 timeline arrows point right; "Asynchronous" centred under the cloud centre line.

🎯 **What:** The vulnerability fixed
Fixed a command injection vulnerability in `crepuscularity-cli/src/benchmark.rs:run_shell` where untrusted benchmark scripts were passed inline to `cmd.exe /C` on Windows, allowing escape sequences or special characters to execute arbitrary commands.

⚠️ **Risk:** The potential impact if left unfixed
Untrusted benchmark files (like `benchmark.toml`) could execute arbitrary malicious commands with the privileges of the user running `crepus benchmark`. This allows attackers to compromise the host machine if users run benchmarks from untrusted repositories.

🛡️ **Solution:** How the fix addresses the vulnerability
Instead of passing the script string directly to `cmd /C`, the script is now written to a uniquely named, temporary batch file (`.bat`) inside the working directory, which is then safely executed and immediately deleted regardless of exit status. This bypasses the dangerous parsing behavior of `cmd.exe` entirely.

## What
Replaces the single-EC2 + `docker-compose` + `setup.sh` UserData template with a **fully declarative CloudFormation stack** — the "less script, more smart vars" ask, mirroring what we did to the Railway template.

## Architecture
- **ECS/Fargate** managed containers: `gateway` (:8787), `optimizer` (:8088, internal), `proxy`/console (:3000), wired by **ECS Service Connect** so the proxy's baked bare upstreams (`gateway:8787`, `optimizer:8088`) resolve with dynamic task IPs (sidesteps the stale-IP nginx resolver problem).
- **RDS PostgreSQL** (managed) replaces the volume-baked Postgres + its drift hazard. The gateway DB URL is **composed** from the RDS endpoint + RDS-managed password into a Secrets Manager secret (a custom resource), injected into both `ANYRAY_SPEND_DB_URL` and `ANYRAY_OBSERVABILITY_DB_URL`.
- **EFS** access points at `/data` for gateway + optimizer → runtime config (routing, optimizer strategy, entitlement lease) survives task restarts.
- **ALB** fronts :8787 + :3000, scoped to `AllowedCidr`; optional `CertificateArn` upgrades both listeners to HTTPS. HTTP by default — parity with the old template (which was already `http://`).

author: alihamzaazam
body:
First of the phased audit PRs — **security**.

## What & why
The remote WebSocket bridge forwarded the *entire* local RPC dispatch, and `agent.adopt` shell-injected its `session_id` (run via `sh -c` by tmux) — together a **remote-reachable RCE**.

- **`agent.adopt` (rpc.rs):** validate `session_id` to `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` and `shell_quote` it; reject crafted ids. (`agent.spawn` already quoted its task.)
- **Remote bridge (remote.rs):** strict **default-deny** method allowlist — only read + interaction with *existing* agents and the companion's own push registration. Host-management (repo/lane/worktree mutation, agent spawn/adopt/stop, config writes, terminal/fs, `daemon.shutdown`) is rejected over the network. The local Unix socket is unaffected.
- **Remote bridge:** explicit WebSocket message/frame size limits + a concurrent-connection cap.
- **Push (store + push.rs):** cap registered devices to the newest `MAX_DEVICES` (evict oldest); send APNs concurrently (bounded) instead of serially.
- **Shell strings (claude.rs/config.rs):** `shell_quote` the `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` path; validate `config.tmux_session` to `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` at load (reset to default on bad input, no hard fail).

## Tests
TDD throughout: `session_id` validator (injection rejected), remote allowlist allow/deny table, `tmux_session` validation + fallback, device-cap eviction. Full workspace suite green (incl. the remote integration test, updated to expect `ping`/`repo.list` allowed).

`tools/` is **not** an npm workspace (workspaces glob is `packages/*`), so the TypeScript build, lint, tests and Docker images never touch it. It's a host-only, run-by-hand tool. No code in `packages/**` changes, so this is a docs/tooling-only PR.

MetaData cache held a pre-migration sessions table (`AttributeError: session_type`).

  tied to a ground-truth source page; `--questions-per-page` for density).

author: tonywangcn
body:
Adds `--buckets N` to `cc merge`: a memory-safe 2-stage hash-partitioned merge for full-scale panels.

## Why
A single-pass `cc merge` over a 100M+-domain panel runs one giant `GROUP BY` with a per-row crawl join. The string aggregates (`arg_max`/`min`/`max` over ~170M groups) overshoot `memory_limit` and can swap-thrash a small or shared box.

## What
`--buckets N` runs a 2-stage merge:
1. **Partition** — stream the panel into N hash buckets on disk (constant memory, ZSTD — the snappy default nearly doubled size and filled the volume).
2. **Aggregate** — each bucket independently, with **no per-row join** (crawl string as the order key, then a post-join to the ~80-row crawl→ord map).

Output is a directory `<out>/part-*.parquet`, readable as a glob by `cc sample`/`cc analyze`. Single-pass stays the default for small panels.

## Verification
- Unit tests for both SQL builders (`TestBuildPartitionSQL`, `TestBuildBucketAggSQL`).
- End-to-end on a synthetic 4-crawl panel: single-pass and `--buckets 4` produce **identical labels** across all four classes (alive_present / dead_candidate / dark_ambiguous / intermittent).

This is the merge mode used to build the 172.96M-domain dead-web-commoncrawl panel.

author: zhaoyue722
body:
Implements the drift detection we agreed on, so a stale `pricing_overrides.json` entry can't silently mask correct LiteLLM prices again (the deepseek-v4-pro 4× overcharge in #49 is the poster child).

## What it does

`detect_override_drift()` compares every override entry against the **raw** LiteLLM catalog and classifies it:

| kind | meaning | CI |
|---|---|---|
| **redundant** | pinned price now matches LiteLLM | **fails** — delete the entry |
| **diverged** | pin differs from LiteLLM (intentional) | passes, **warns** with the per-field delta |
| **gap_fill** | LiteLLM doesn't carry the model | passes — override is the only source |

Precedence is unchanged: `override > LiteLLM`, field-level. This only *surfaces* staleness; it doesn't change how prices resolve.

## Where the check runs

In `tests/test_pricing_drift.py` (so it runs in the existing CI quality-gate on every PR — including the weekly pricing-refresh PR, which is exactly when someone's looking at pricing). The catalog guard fails on redundant overrides; diverged ones become pytest warnings (visible in the CI summary) prompting a reviewer to re-confirm the pin.

## Metadata

Override entries may carry optional `_reason` / `_added` keys to document *why* they exist. The loader (`parse_litellm_entry`) and the drift check both ignore any `_`-prefixed field, so it's free annotation. Documented in `pricing_data/README.md`.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests: redundant / diverged (with delta) / gap_fill / `_`-metadata-ignored / no-price-field.
- [x] Real-file guard passes (overrides are currently empty post-#49).
- [x] `uv run pytest` 711 passed; ruff + format + mypy clean.

body:
Addresses two Low-severity findings from the latest review pass, grouped as the config-hardening PR.

## Finding #4 — scalar parsers silently ignored trailing tokens

`external`, `logformat`, `dns.prefer`, and the `dns.cachettl`/`auth.cachettl` `off|none|disabled` keyword each read only `vals[0]`, so a typo like `logformat: json text` or `external: 0.0.0.0 oops` was silently accepted using just the first token. (The numeric/boolean/endpoint settings were tightened in #35; these were the stragglers.)

They now route through the existing `expect_single` helper, so they require exactly one value — consistent with the rest of the parser. The numeric `cache_ttl` branch already went through `parse_u64` → `expect_single`; only its keyword branch needed the guard.

## Finding #5 — `u64 as usize` truncation on 32-bit

`maxconnections` and `logrotate.keep` were cast `u64 as usize` *before* their range checks, which wraps a value above `usize::MAX` on a 32-bit target.

- `maxconnections` now uses the existing `parse_usize_positive` (which does `usize::try_from` + rejects `0`).
- A new `parse_usize` (zero allowed, `try_from`) backs `logrotate.keep`, and `parse_usize_positive` now delegates to it.

## Tests

- New `rejects_trailing_tokens_on_value_settings` parser test covering `external`/`logformat`/`dns.prefer`/`dns.cachettl`/`auth.cachettl`/`logrotate.keep` (both the rejected-trailing-token and valid single-value forms).
- The truncation guard can't be triggered on a 64-bit host (`usize == u64`), so it's correct by construction via `usize::try_from` rather than unit-tested.

Full suite green, clippy and fmt clean. No behavior change for valid configs.

body:
Small workspace lint + profile hardening, following the unwrap-discipline work in #438.

## Lints
- **`unreachable_pub = "warn"`** (rustc) — flags `pub` items not reachable from the crate root, keeping internal APIs honestly scoped instead of leaking a wider surface than callers can use. Measured blast radius up front: **2 production sites** (`mkit-git-bridge::b64::{encode,decode}` → `pub(crate)`) and ~27 test-only helpers in `tests/common/` (→ `pub(crate)`). All fixed here.
- **`clippy::dbg_macro = "deny"`** — a stray `dbg!()` must never ship (zero in the tree today, so no fixes — this just keeps it that way).

## Doc correctness
- `clippy.toml`: the comment claimed both `unwrap_used`/`expect_used` are denied. Only `unwrap_used` is — `expect("reason")` is deliberately the sanctioned panic path (carries a reason). Comment corrected to match.

## Release profile: `panic = "unwind"` (was `"abort"`)
Production bans `unwrap()` and uses `expect("reason")`, so a panic is rare and meaningful — keeping unwinding in release means it yields a real backtrace for users instead of an opaque abort. Added a byte-deterministic **`[profile.reproducible]`** (`panic = "abort"`, no unwinding tables — the main source of toolchain drift in a rebuild-and-hash check) for a future reproducible-build pipeline to target. (No consumer wired yet; both `catch_unwind` sites in the tree are in tests, which already build with unwind, so nothing depended on release `abort`.)

## Verification
`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` clean (the CI gate); affected-crate tests pass (`mkit-git-bridge`, `mkit-keystore`, `mkit-cli` integration). fmt clean.

body:
## Problem

`runPreLaunchSync` (`CustomPlayButton.tsx`) only branched on `!result.success && result.errors?.length > 0`. Backend failures with `success: false` but **no `errors`** key fall through to `"proceed"` with zero user signal: `DEVICE_NOT_REGISTERED`, `save_sort_changed` (whose "migrate saves in Settings first" message was never shown), `blocked_by_migration`. The user plays on stale local saves believing pre-launch sync ran; post-exit then produces avoidable conflicts. `handleResolveConflict` had the same hole — it only branched on `conflicts`, so a `success: false` with no conflicts dispatched a refresh and dropped to `"play"` as if resolved.

## Fix

Both paths now branch on `!result.success`:

- **`runPreLaunchSync`**: any resolved failure routes through the existing fallback-launch confirm ("Launch with local saves?"). `confirmFallbackLaunch` takes an optional `message` so the backend's specific reason is surfaced — `save_sort_changed`'s "migrate saves in Settings first" is finally shown. The benign `savefiles_in_content_dir` skip still returns **early** (before the new branch), so it stays a silent no-op — no per-launch nag.
- **`handleResolveConflict`**: a `success: false` without conflicts stays in the conflict state and toasts the message, instead of masquerading as resolved.

## Tests

`CustomPlayButton.test.tsx` — for each no-errors shape (`device_not_registered` / `save_sort_changed` / `blocked_by_migration`): the fallback confirm opens (not a silent launch) and its description surfaces the backend message; cancelling does not launch (`RunGame` not called), confirming does. Plus a resolve-conflict test: `success:false` without conflicts → stays "Resolve Conflict" and toasts the message. Full frontend suite green (1262 tests).

## Docs

`docs: N/A` — internal robustness fix. A failed pre-launch/resolve now surfaces a confirm / toast instead of silently proceeding; no backend change, no new flow.

body:
## Summary

Answers the **first open question** of `cayley-hamilton-minpoly-oq-06` ("similar matrices share a minimal polynomial"): *formalize the minimal polynomial together with the invariant factors (rational canonical form).*

The rational canonical form writes a matrix as a block-diagonal sum of companion matrices `C(f₁) ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ C(f_k)` with invariant factors `f₁ ∣ ⋯ ∣ f_k`. The classical **readout** recovers the matrix's two distinguished polynomials: `charpoly = ∏ fᵢ` (product) and `minpoly = f_k` (largest). This PR proves the readout for the **two-invariant-factor case**, stated for arbitrary *nonderogatory* blocks (so it applies verbatim to companion matrices).

## New content (sorry-free, axiom-free)

`#print axioms` → only `propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound`.

- **`aeval_fromBlocks`** — polynomial evaluation distributes over a block-diagonal matrix: `q(A ⊕ D) = q(A) ⊕ q(D)`, by polynomial induction (helper `algebraMap_fromBlocks` splits the scalar matrix into block-diagonal scalar blocks).
- **`minpoly_fromBlocks_of_dvd`** — when `minpoly A ∣ minpoly D`, `minpoly (A ⊕ D) = minpoly D`. This is the **minimal-polynomial counterpart of Mathlib's `charpoly_fromBlocks_zero₁₂`**, which is *missing from Mathlib v4.26.0*. Proved by two-way divisibility (annihilation + reading off the bottom-right block), no module theory or `lcm` bookkeeping.
- **`rcf_two_invariant_factors`** — for nonderogatory blocks (`minpoly = charpoly =` invariant factor) with `f₁ ∣ f₂`: `charpoly (A ⊕ D) = f₁·f₂` and `minpoly (A ⊕ D) = f₂`. The gallery's existing `charpoly(C f) = minpoly(C f) = f` (in `CayleyHamiltonReductionOQ02OQ01`) instantiates the hypotheses with companion matrices.

## Scope / honesty

This is the **readout** direction of RCF. The general `k`-factor case needs a `Sigma`-indexed block matrix (companion blocks of differing degrees do not fit Mathlib's uniform `blockDiagonal`), and the **existence** of the invariant-factor decomposition (the PID module-structure theorem, ~800 lines) is independent — both left as documented open questions.

author: danypm
body:
## Problem

Production logs showed clusters of `WH user reengagement near-miss` plus `Notification process took too long: 5m12s`. The daily JORF notification run was pushing WhatsApp users out of their 24h window — sometimes while still **inside** it (e.g. elapsed 23h57m, "missed by 2m39s", yet flagged expired). Those users got a **paid re-engagement template** when a **free in-window message** was still legal.

### Root cause

Three things lined up (the matching ~5-minute timings were causal, not coincidental):

1. **Per-handler clock drift.** Each of the 5 notification handlers computed its own `now = new Date()` per task. Over a 5m+ run the clock drifts (logs show `08:05:38` in one handler, `08:09:42` in another, same run) — a user judged in-window by the first handler is judged expired by the last.
2. **Margin == process latency.** The 5-min safety margin was fully consumed by the 5m12s run, so it protected nothing.
3. **One overloaded constant.** `WHATSAPP_REENGAGEMENT_MARGIN_MINS` drove the cutoff margin, the near-miss window, **and** the scheduler day-of-week step at once.

## Changes

- **Single window clock**: `runNotificationProcess` snapshots one `windowNow` and threads it through `notifyAllFollows` into all 5 handlers; per-task `new Date()` removed. The 24h decision is now stable regardless of run duration.
- **Edge-first WhatsApp dispatch**: sort the WhatsApp batch by `lastEngagementAt` ascending so users nearest their window edge are sent in the run's first seconds and keep the benefit of the scheduler's day-of-week start-advance. Other apps still sort by record count.
- **Constant split**: add `WHATSAPP_SHIFT_STEP_MINS` so the scheduler step is independent of the cutoff margin. **Day-of-week shift behavior is unchanged** (it is the intended retention mechanism) — values can now be tuned separately from data.

## Tests

- `10.notificationDispatch` — edge-first WhatsApp ordering; non-WhatsApp unchanged.
- `11.notification.window` — handler honors injected `windowNow` for expiry + near-miss, not wall-clock.
- `12.notificationScheduler` — day-of-week shift uses `WHATSAPP_SHIFT_STEP_MINS`; no shift for non-WhatsApp.

## Test-suite flakiness (fixed)

A prior `tsc` build emits `dist/tests/*.test.js` and `dist/**/*.js`. vitest was running every suite **twice** (source + compiled copy), racing the two on the shared in-memory MongoDB (`dropDatabase` wiping the other mid-test); eslint was parse-erroring on `dist/` output. Scoped vitest to `tests/` and ignored `dist/` in eslint. Full suite now deterministic: **195 passed, 0 failed**.

## Verification

- `npm run build` (tsc): clean
- `npx vitest run`: 195 passed / 0 failed
- `npx eslint .`: no issues

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

After a week of data, retune `WHATSAPP_REENGAGEMENT_MARGIN_MINS` (likely 5→~2, more free messages) and the shift step.

author: chrisdok43
body:
## Summary

The `gpu` entitlement was unusable on **JetPack 5 / L4T r35** Jetsons (worked on JP6). Inside the container `libcuda.so.1` was a 0-byte stub (host driver never bind-mounted) and the Tegra iGPU device nodes were missing → `torch.cuda.is_available() == False`.

**Root cause:** the device's `nvidia-container-toolkit` (≤1.11 — `1.11.0-rc.1` on the Go2 Orin) predates `nvidia-ctk cdi generate`, so the agent's CDI generation fails and **no CDI spec is ever produced**. `applyCDIGPU` then mounts nothing and the container falls back to discrete-GPU device nodes only — no `libcuda.so.1` mount, no iGPU nodes. JP6 works because its newer toolkit produces a real CDI spec.

## Fix

Add an in-agent **L4T "CSV mode" fallback**. When no `nvidia-ctk` CDI spec is available, translate the device's own NVIDIA Container Runtime CSV file lists (`/etc/nvidia-container-runtime/host-files-for-container.d/*.csv`) directly into OCI mounts and device nodes:

- `lib` / `sym` / `dir` → read-only bind-mount at the same path (overlays the image's 0-byte `libcuda.so.1` stub with the real 23 MB host driver). `noexec` is deliberately omitted so the loader can mmap libraries executable.
- `dev` → device node + cgroup allow rule (`/dev/nvmap`, `/dev/nvhost-*`, the full `/dev/nvgpu/igpu0/*` set).
- Missing sources are skipped so a stale CSV entry can't block container start.

These CSVs already ship on the affected images, so GPU works on the device **as-is — no toolkit upgrade, no reflash**. JP6 keeps using its real CDI spec (fallback only triggers when none exists).

Also adds `oci.DedupeDevices`, run before the spec is serialized: the GPU setup (CDI or CSV) and the `gpu` entitlement can both add the same node (e.g. `/dev/nvidiactl`), and runc `mknod()`s each entry, so a duplicate path would fail container creation with `EEXIST`. This also hardens the pre-existing CDI path.

## Files

- `go/internal/agent/cdi/csv.go` (+ `csv_test.go`) — `ApplyL4TCSV` and CSV parsing
- `go/internal/agent/containerd/client.go` — wire the fallback into `applyCDIGPU`; dedup before serialize
- `go/internal/agent/oci/spec.go` (+ `dedupe_test.go`) — `DedupeDevices`

## Testing

- Unit: `oci` + `cdi` packages pass (incl. `-race`); `gofmt`/`go vet` clean; linux/arm64 agent builds.
- **Verified end-to-end on a real JetPack-5 Go2** (WendyOS, JP5.1.1) — side-loaded the agent, recreated the gpu container:

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `…/tegra/libcuda.so.1` | 0 bytes (stub) | **23,217,008 bytes** (real driver) |
| `/dev/nvmap`, `/dev/nvhost-gpu`, `/dev/nvgpu` | missing | **present** |
| `torch.cuda.is_available()` | False | **True — "Orin"** |
| go2-initial-test **gpu** tile | FAIL | **PASS** — `Orin · CUDA 11.4 · 2k×2k matmul 50.8 ms` |
| go2-initial-test **jetson** tile | FAIL (TensorRT ImportError) | **PASS** — `TensorRT 8.5.2.2` |

Fixes WDY-1716
